rubric.criterion: The reviewer does not edit the fixture.
The review reconstructs the observation, missing-data, incident, notification, and recovery lifecycle from input to operator-visible result.
The reviewer identifies that monitor state and status presentation independently decide whether the same sensor is missing.
The reviewer challenges caller-owned coordination across health, incident, and notification state and recommends one semantic owner for the transition.
The reviewer compares the current system with a smaller behavior-first shape whose views derive from one authoritative transition path.
The report is organized under a descriptive monitoring feature heading rather than a numbered list of findings.
Current and proposed architecture diagrams assign every fact, transition, persistence boundary, and external effect to an owner.
Pseudocode makes the proposed normal, duplicate, notification-failure, and recovery paths concrete enough to evaluate.
The reviewer recommends one target shape, explains why it is smaller and more correct than the current system, and names the material tradeoff or rejected alternative.
The branch receives REDESIGN rather than a list of local cleanup suggestions.
The target preserves one incident per missing episode, durable notification intent, explicit delivery failure, and recovery.
